summary: Lomé–Tokoin International Airport (LFW) is the principal international gateway of Togo, located about 5 km northeast of the capital city Lomé along the Gulf of Guinea coast. It serves as the main hub for ASKY Airlines and Ethiopian Airlines' West African operations, connecting the country to destinations across Africa, Europe, and the Middle East. The airport handles the majority of Togo's international air traffic and features a single modern terminal serving both domestic and international flights.
faqs:
Q: How far is the airport from central Lomé?
A: The airport is approximately 5 km (3 miles) from the city center, typically a 15-20 minute drive depending on traffic conditions.

Q: Which airlines operate from Lomé–Tokoin International Airport?
A: Major carriers include ASKY Airlines, Ethiopian Airlines, Royal Air Maroc, Air France, Brussels Airlines, and TAP Air Portugal, among others.

Q: Does the airport offer international flights?
A: Yes, the airport handles numerous international routes connecting Togo to destinations throughout Africa, Europe, and the Middle East.

Q: Are there currency exchange services at the airport?
A: Yes, currency exchange facilities are available in the terminal for converting major currencies to West African CFA franc (XOF), the local currency.
transport_tips: Taxis are the most common way to reach the airport; agree on the fare in advance as meters are rarely used. Shared shuttle services and hotel transfers are also available through many accommodations in Lomé. The main road connecting the airport to the city center passes through the Tokoin neighborhood and is generally well-maintained.
local_tip: If you have a layover or extra time, consider visiting the Lomé Grand Market (Marché des Nana Benz) nearby, known for vibrant fabrics and traditional Togolese textiles—bargaining is expected and part of the experience.
